pairs.why: Both are the same flat disc, but A's saturated teal body reads more like the rich, candy-colored toy objects in the real cards than B's plain gray-white metal.
B is a properly built saucer with a full rounded rim, lights wrapped around the side and a purple underside, matching the chunky volume of the real cards, while A is a thin flat plate.
B is built like a real astronaut helmet with ear pieces and panel seams, while A is a glossy striped ball on a plinth that looks like a toy statue.
A is a plain glossy white sphere that reads like a statue, while B has real helmet construction and the soft, slightly satin finish of the real cards.
B's navy-and-gold refractor on a wooden tripod is built more believably and sits in the scene like the real binoculars, though A's chunky shapes are also close.
A looks flat and dull in dusty brown, while B has the smooth, painterly finish, cool saturated palette and believable dome-and-tunnel build of the real scene cards.
B's glowing door, warm lit interior, saturated colors and inviting cartoon-scene look match the lighthouse and motel cards better than A's colder gray render.
The two are almost identical in build, palette and finish; B is only marginally crisper, which is not a real difference.
